cards.method: Realized (co)variance & intraday spot volatility from high-frequency data
cards.when: you have intraday data and you want the ex-post realized volatility/covariance of ONE day (rCov=the sum of r², the jump-robust rBPCov/medRV, the noise-robust rKernelCov/rTSCov), a semivariance decomposition, or an intraday spot-volatility pattern
cards.when_not: daily or low-frequency series -> a parametric GARCH (#28/#154); conditional or forecast volatility -> GARCH; a multi-day dynamic covariance -> DCC (#29/#155); you have no intraday observations

alternatives.criterion: conditional/forecast volatility from daily returns rather than an ex-post realized measure
a dynamic multi-day correlation/covariance rather than a per-day realized covariance
suspected jumps in the intraday series (a jump-robust integrated variance)
market microstructure noise (bid-ask bounce) -> noise-robust estimators
you want downside/upside (negative/positive/mixed/concordant) semicovariance

output_key_fields: hf_realized_var: realized_variance (the scalar sum or a robust version) + realized_vol=sqrt; K (rTSCov only); n_obs/n_returns
hf_realized_cov: rcov (the N×N covariance, or the correlation when cor=True); correlation (derived from the covariance when cor=False); asset_names; n_assets
hf_realized_cov with measure=rSemiCov: semicov=list{mixed,negative,positive,concordant} N×N + rcov (=the sum)
hf_spot_vol: spot_vol (the numeric intraday series); timestamps; daily (per day); periodic (the intraday pattern); n_na
interpretation_traps: the multivariate two-scale covariance requires a LIST of per-asset series; a single multi-column input reduces SILENTLY to a scalar — the wrapper handles that, so do not bypass it
measure='medRV' -> rMedRVar (rMedRV is deprecated in 1.0.3)
the two-scale and kernel covariances require PRICES (the returns are formed internally); the two-scale estimator needs n>=10*K, otherwise the gate stops
alignBy is NOT exposed for the realized measures: the data must ALREADY be sampled (e.g. 5-min) intraday data for ONE day; the value is timestamp-invariant without alignBy
spotVol with method='detPer' ideally wants >=50 days; fewer -> a warning (unstable periodicity), not an error; read n_na
realized variance ≠ conditional/forecast variance: it is an ex-post estimate of one day's integrated variance, not a forecast

Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys 2003 (Econometrica 71:579) — realized volatility
Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2004 (J. Financial Econometrics) — bipower variation (rBPCov)
Andersen, Dobrev & Schaumburg 2012 (J. Econometrics 169:75) — MedRV, jump-robust

Bollerslev, Li, Patton & Quaedvlieg 2020 (J. Econometrics 217:411) — realized semicovariance (rSemiCov)
Boudt, Croux & Laurent 2011 (J. Empirical Finance 18:353) — deterministic periodicity spot vol (spotVol detPer)

cards.method: HAR realized-volatility models (HAR/HARJ/HARQ/HARQ-J) — estimation, rolling OOS forecasting, simulation
cards.when: you have a daily realized measure (realized variance/RV) of an integrated volatility and you want to model its long-memory dynamics with the heterogeneous autoregressive (HAR) model of Corsi (2009); a daily/weekly/monthly cascade (c(1,5,22)); jump-robust (HARJ) or measurement-error-corrected (HARQ)
cards.when_not: you only have daily returns without a realized measure -> #28/#154; you want multivariate or conditional-correlation volatility -> #29/#155; regime-switching volatility -> #31; the intraday realized measure must be computed FIRST (#156, hf_realized_var)

alternatives.criterion: only daily returns are available (no realized measure); a parametric conditional variance
significant jumps -> separate the continuous (BPV) from the jump component
measurement error in the RV -> a correction with the realized quarticity (BPQ 2016)
you want to link the volatility to a low-frequency macro variable (GARCH-MIDAS)

output_key_fields: coefficients: a named vector (beta0, the intercept, plus one beta per period); coef_table: Estimate/Std.Error/t/p from the least-squares summary
r_squared/adj_r_squared/sigma/log_lik: fit diagnostics; qlike_mean: the QLIKE loss (the main volatility-forecast loss); qlike: the per-observation vector
uncond_mean: the unconditional mean volatility (type='HAR' ONLY; blank elsewhere — it is not defined for the other types)
fitted/residuals: chart-data; nobs/type/periods: metadata
har_forecast: forecast (the getForc vector); forecast_matrix (step×roll); actual (forecastComparison); forecast_residuals; rmse/mae; an object of class HARForecast
har_simulate: simulation (a numeric vector); an object of class HARSim (object@simulation)
interpretation_traps: RM is a realized VARIANCE (not returns, not a standard deviation) and must be a positive series; gaps are accepted silently by the routine -> an explicit gate blocks them
an invalid type returns nothing SILENTLY (it only prints a message); the wrapper fences it with a closed enum {HAR, HARJ, HARQ, HARQ-J}
HARJ/HARQ-J require BPV; HARQ/HARQ-J require RQ (of the same length as RM); without them -> a cryptic armadillo error, the wrapper gives a clean gate
QLIKE (qlike_mean) is the appropriate robust volatility-forecast loss (Patton 2011); NOT an MSE on the levels — prefer it for model comparison
uncond_mean is returned ONLY for HAR (blank for HARJ/HARQ/HARQ-J); the model handle is a plain least-squares fit of the HAR components
length(RM) must be >= max(periods)+2, otherwise an armadillo error; the wrapper fences it
sources: Corsi F. 2009, 'A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility', Journal of Financial Econometrics 7(2):174-196
Bollerslev, Patton & Quaedvlieg 2016, 'Exploiting the errors: A simple approach for improved volatility forecasting', Journal of Econometrics 192(1):1-18 (HARQ/HARQ-J)
Patton A. 2011, 'Volatility forecast comparison using imperfect volatility proxies', Journal of Econometrics 160(1):246-256 (QLIKE)

cards.method: Generalized Autoregressive Score / Dynamic Conditional Score (GAS/DCS) — a time-varying volatility/location/tails
cards.when: one univariate series with score-driven dynamics in a parameter (variance/mean/tails); an explicit distribution (norm/t/ged/gamma..); an alternative to GARCH with a full distributional likelihood
cards.when_not: multivariate volatility or correlation -> #29/#155/#160; variance-only dynamics through the standard GARCH interface -> #28/#154; regime switching -> #31/#30; realized or intraday volatility -> #156

alternatives.criterion: you want a classic GARCH-family variance model with the standard interface/rolling backtest
a modern (m)GARCH; multivariate DCC/copula volatility

output_key_fields: coef_table: a matrix Estimate/Std. Error/z value/Pr(>|z|) of the coefficients (omega/alpha/phi per parameter)
par_tv / mean_tv / var_tv: the time-varying parameters / mean / VARIANCE (chart-data; var_tv = the volatility path when par_static drives the variance)
resid_tv / score_tv / loglik_tv: standardized residuals, the score path, the per-observation log-likelihood
loglik_sum / aic / bic: fit criteria; converged + status_optim/status_hessian: convergence (a stateless node — do not ignore them)
gas_forecast: y_ahead_mean (+ y_ahead_sd/y_ahead_quant with simulated_paths = a fan chart); gas_simulate: y_sim/par_tv_sim
interpretation_traps: the DEFAULT drives the MEAN (par_static=[False, True] for the normal); for a volatility model you MUST set par_static=[1,0] so that the VARIANCE is the dynamic parameter
converged=False (for instance status_optim='iteration_limit_reached') => the estimates are NOT reliable; the bounded evaluation budget yields converged=False rather than a hang
the fisher_* scaling options are MUCH heavier (a numerical Fisher matrix); unit is the safe default; for orthogonal distributions the scaling variants coincide
quant under simulated_paths are quantiles of the PREDICTIVE distribution (a fan chart); mean_path gives only a point forecast (no y_ahead_quant)
gas_forecast(simulated_paths)/gas_simulate are stochastic -> seeded internally (default 2025) for determinism; positive distributions require y>0 (a hard gate)

cards.method: GARCH-MIDAS (a short-run GARCH × a long-run MIDAS macro component)
cards.when: you want to link the volatility of high-frequency returns (y) to a slow macro variable (x; e.g. industrial production, the NFCI) through MIDAS; the volatility = tau_t (long run, macro-driven) × g_t (short-run GARCH). mfg_fit -> mfg_predict; mfg_simulate = a standalone DGP
cards.when_not: a purely univariate GARCH with no exogenous macro driver -> #28/#154; regime-switching volatility -> #31; multivariate work -> #29/#155; you have no low-frequency variable that stays constant within each period

alternatives.criterion: there is no macro long-run driver; a plain univariate GARCH
a regime change (not a slow macro trend) drives the volatility
you want free (non-monotone) MIDAS weighting -> an extra w1 parameter

output_key_fields: par: a named vector of estimates (mu/alpha/beta/gamma/m/theta/w2[+w1 in the unrestricted case])
coefficients: a frame of estimate/rob_std_err/p_value/opg_std_err/opg_p_value
tau: the long-run component (chart); g: the short-run component (chart); tau×g = the total variance
variance_ratio: the share of variance explained by the long-run component; tau_forecast: the one-step long-run value
llh/bic; convergence (the integer optim code); converged (logical)
interpretation_traps: silent non-convergence: optim RETURNS a fit even when convergence!=0 — CHECK the converged field before interpreting
x MUST be constant within each low_freq period; mixed values trip the 'a SINGLE unique value' gate (not a silent error)
a column literally NAMED 'date' with a date dtype is mandatory, AND the low_freq column must be a date as well; otherwise it is blocked
K must be smaller than the number of low_freq periods (otherwise the MIDAS lag builds negative-length vectors)
beta_restricted pins w1=1 (a monotonically decreasing weighting); beta_unrestricted adds a free w1 parameter
mfg_predict returns the total conditional variance per horizon (not tau or g separately)
sources: Engle, Ghysels & Sohn 2013 'Stock Market Volatility and Macroeconomic Fundamentals' (REStat 95:776)
Conrad & Kleen 2020 'Two are better than one: Volatility forecasting using multiplicative component GARCH-MIDAS' (J. Applied Econometrics 35:19)
Ghysels, Santa-Clara & Valkanov 2004/2006 (MIDAS regressions)

cards.method: BEKK-family multivariate GARCH (BEKK/diagonal/scalar) + multivariate VaR + Volatility IRF
cards.when: N-dimensional returns; you want the full BEKK dynamic conditional covariance (spillovers/co-volatility) + risk (a portfolio VaR) or volatility impulse responses
cards.when_not: a large N (BEKK carries roughly O(N²) parameters -> the curse of dimensionality; go to DCC, #155/#29); a univariate series (-> #28); you need an asymmetric VIRF (not implemented)

alternatives.criterion: a large N / you want a scalable conditional correlation rather than a full BEKK
fewer parameters (diagonal/scalar) when the full BEKK is not identified
a non-model-based (historical/gaussian/modified) VaR without MGARCH dynamics

output_key_fields: bekk_valid: a boolean — True = a stationary, valid BEKK; False = degenerate (the VaR and VIRF are unreliable)
log_likelihood/AIC/BIC: fit criteria; theta: the estimated parameters (vech)
C0/A/G: the BEKK parameter matrices (C0 the lower-triangular intercept, A the ARCH matrix, G the GARCH matrix)
sigma_t: the T×N(N+1)/2 conditional st.dev/covariance path (chart-data)
var_values (bekk_var): the T×1 (portfolio) or T×N (per-series) VaR path
virf/virf_upper/virf_lower (bekk_virf): n_ahead × N(N+1)/2 responses + bands
interpretation_traps: bekk_valid=False is NOT blocked (a valid output with a flag, since the node is stateless): always read it before using the VaR or VIRF
VaR with distribution='empirical' requires >=1000 observations (gated); the default is 'normal' — switch to 't' for fat tails
the VIRF exists only for a SYMMETRIC BEKK (asymmetric=False); an asymmetric fit is blocked by a gate
portfolio_weights left unset gives a per-series VaR (N columns); a vector of length N gives a portfolio VaR (1 column)
the BEKK curse of dimensionality: ~O(N²) parameters; for N>~4 prefer DCC (#155/#29)
sources: Engle & Kroner 1995 (Econometric Theory 11:122) — the BEKK parameterisation
Hafner & Herwartz 2006 (J. Int. Money & Finance 25:719) — Volatility Impulse Responses

cards.method: (Hierarchical) Hidden Markov Models + Viterbi global decoding + forecasting
cards.when: a univariate series (returns/observations) with latent discrete regimes; you want a full HMM with probabilistic state-dependent distributions (normal/t/gamma/..) + decoding of the most likely state sequence
cards.when_not: regime-conditional GARCH volatility (-> #31, msg_fit_*); a linear Markov-switching model with regressors (-> #30, ms_fit); threshold (self-exciting) non-Markovian regimes (-> #32, setar_fit); hierarchical two-level data (the hierarchy switch is not exposed)

alternatives.criterion: the regimes concern volatility clustering (the conditional variance), not the level/mean
a Markov-switching linear model with exogenous regressors
the regimes are determined by an observable threshold variable, not by a latent Markov chain
fat tails in the returns within a regime

output_key_fields: hmm_fit: log_lik/AIC/BIC/npar/nobs; estimates (a data_frame parameter/lb/estimate/ub — the Gamma_ij transitions + mu/sigma/df per state); nstates/sdd
hmm_fit convergence: nlm_code (1/2=OK); converged (bool); n_accepted_runs — check them BEFORE interpreting (a stateless node: stderr is lost)
hmm_decode: states (an integer sequence of length T); state_counts/state_labels; n_states_used; degenerate (True => fewer than nstates were actually used)
hmm_predict: state_probs (ahead × nstates probabilities); forecast (ahead × {lb,estimate,ub} observations); it decodes internally (predict requires it)
interpretation_traps: state labelling is not inherently ordered (label switching); identify the states through the mu/sigma in estimates, not through the index 1/2
degenerate=True or converged=False => the solution collapsed or did not converge — do NOT interpret the regimes; raise the number of runs or change the state-dependent distribution
AIC/BIC are comparable ONLY on the same data & sdd family (a different nstates is nested; a different sdd is non-nested)
gamma/lognormal require strictly positive values, poisson non-negative integers — for raw returns use normal/t
the artificial date column is a placeholder the fitter requires; it does not affect the estimation, so do not read it as a real calendar
sources: Oelschläger, Adam & Michels 2024 JSS (hidden Markov models for financial time series)
Zucchini, MacDonald & Langrock 2016, 'Hidden Markov Models for Time Series' 2nd ed. (Viterbi global decoding §5)
Hamilton 1989 (Econometrica 57:357) Markov-switching regimes
precondition_tools: hmm_fit (the PRODUCER; check converged/n_accepted_runs before decode/predict)
hmm_decode (the degenerate flag: did the fit fall back to fewer than k states?)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the series from a file, if needed)

cards.method: Bayesian univariate Stochastic Volatility (vanilla / Student-t / leverage) via MCMC
cards.when: a univariate return series; you want the latent (unobserved) volatility as a stochastic process with a full Bayesian posterior (uncertainty bands on the volatility), not a deterministic GARCH-type recursion
cards.when_not: you want a point or ML volatility estimate, or closed-form forecasting -> #28/#154; multivariate volatility or correlation -> #29/#155; regime-switching volatility -> #31; very large samples on a tight latency budget (the MCMC is expensive)

alternatives.criterion: you want a deterministic ML GARCH with closed-form forecasts rather than latent-SV MCMC
the volatility changes regime (Markov switching) rather than following a continuous AR(1) log-volatility
multivariate volatility + a time-varying correlation
fat tails in the returns beyond what the stochastic volatility delivers
asymmetry: negative returns raise the volatility more (the leverage effect)

output_key_fields: para_summary: a matrix mean/sd/5%/50%/95%/ESS per parameter (mu=the level, phi=persistence, sigma=vol-of-vol, [nu],[rho])
ess / min_ess / converged: the convergence capture — converged=False ⇒ insufficient mixing, do not interpret the posteriors
vol_mean (with vol_time): the posterior mean of exp(h_t/2) per time point (chart data; absent when keeptime='last')
sv_predict: vol_mean/vol_median + vol_lower(5%)/vol_upper(95%) per step — posterior predictive bands of the future volatility
sv_simulate: y (returns) + vol (the true latent volatility) + para — chart-data for a synthetic path
interpretation_traps: check the converged flag first: SV MCMC can silently suffer monstrous autocorrelation (a very low phi ESS); 500 draws is a smoke test — for production raise draws/burnin
phi≈1 ⇒ an almost non-stationary log-volatility (high persistence); phi near 0 ⇒ the volatility is nearly white noise
y is returns (roughly mean-zero), NOT price levels; otherwise the log(y^2) offset produces nonsense
vol_mean refers to exp(h_t/2) (a standard deviation), not a variance; do not compare it directly with a GARCH conditional variance
predict/simulate are stochastic -> seed=2025 by default; the same seed ⇒ the same draws (a reproducible node)
keeptime='last' discards the latent path (vol_mean is absent) — use it only when you do not need the volatility chart
sources: Kastner 2016 JSS 69(5) (dealing with stochastic volatility in time series)
Kastner & Frühwirth-Schnatter (2014) ASIS interweaving (CSDA 76:408) — the sampler behind svsample
Jacquier, Polson & Rossi (1994, JBES 12:371) — the foundations of Bayesian SV
precondition_tools: sv_sample (read converged/min_ess before trusting the posteriors — a low ESS ⇒ raise the number of draws)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (load the return series; NOT price levels)
sv_simulate (a data-generating check / prior predictive check before fitting real data)

cards.method: Multivariate factor stochastic volatility (Bayesian MCMC) + model-implied & predictive covariance/correlation
cards.when: multivariate returns (a small to medium N); you want a time-varying covariance/correlation through a few latent factors with stochastic-volatility dynamics + Bayesian posterior uncertainty
cards.when_not: a univariate series (-> #162, sv_sample); you want a parametric multivariate GARCH point estimate, DCC or GO-GARCH (-> #29/#155); a very large N with no factor structure; too few observations (below roughly 50) for reliable MCMC

alternatives.criterion: you want a parametric DCC/GO-GARCH point-estimate MGARCH rather than a Bayesian factor structure
a univariate series — you do not need a multivariate covariance
you need identification/interpretation of the factor loadings (not only the covariance) — it stabilises the MCMC

output_key_fields: facload_mean (fsv_sample): the posterior-mean matrix of factor loadings (N × factors); it shows which series load on the common factors
communalities / communality_total (fsv_sample): the share of variance per series, and in total, explained by the factors
para_mean (fsv_sample): the posterior-mean mu/phi/sigma of each idiosyncratic and factor log-volatility process (phi -> 1 means high persistence)
ledermann_bound / exceeds_ledermann (fsv_sample): the static bound on identifiable factors; True means take care when interpreting the loadings
cov_mean/cor_mean, with their _sd (fsv_cov): the posterior mean and posterior standard deviation of the conditional covariance and correlation at the last t
pred_cov_mean/pred_cor_mean (fsv_predict): a list of posterior-mean matrices per horizon, keyed by the horizon
interpretation_traps: restrict='none' is preferable for ESTIMATING the covariance/forecast; 'upper' only when you want identifiable/interpretable loadings (a strong a-priori assumption)

exceeds_ledermann=True is NOT an error: the sampler deliberately allows more factors than the static Ledermann bound, since identification comes from the time-varying volatilities; it is a caveat for interpreting the loadings, nothing more
the signs of the factor loadings & factors are not identified by the likelihood (sign switching); interpret magnitudes/patterns, not absolute signs
fsv_cov returns ONLY the last time point (keeptime='last') = the current conditional covariance, not the whole path
MCMC: few draws/burnin -> noise in the posterior; the posterior_sd fields show the uncertainty, do not read only the means
sources: Kastner, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Lopes 2017 JCGS 26(4) (efficient Bayesian inference for multivariate factor stochastic volatility)
Kastner, Frühwirth-Schnatter & Lopes 2017, 'Efficient Bayesian Inference for Multivariate Factor Stochastic Volatility Models', JCGS 26(4):905-917
Kastner 2019, 'Sparse Bayesian time-varying covariance estimation in many dimensions', J. Econometrics 210(1):98-115 (the Normal-Gamma shrinkage prior)
precondition_tools: fsv_cov (the posterior-mean model-implied cov/cor at the last t — a check on plausible magnitudes)
fsv_predict (the posterior predictive h-step cov/cor)

cards.method: Discrete-time Markov chain: estimating the transition matrix (MLE/Laplace/bootstrap CI) + long-run analytics (the stationary distribution, mean first passage times, irreducibility, period)
cards.when: a discrete sequence of states (regimes/ratings/states); you want the estimated transition matrix, the long-run (stationary) distribution, expected first passage times, or an irreducibility/period check
cards.when_not: continuous return or volatility series -> #28/#154; latent regime switching on continuous observations -> #30/#31; a continuous-time Markov chain; higher-order dependence or order selection

alternatives.criterion: the regimes are latent on a continuous observed series, not directly observed states
Markov switching in the variance of continuous returns
a hidden Markov model with emission distributions rather than observed states

output_key_fields: transitionMatrix: the estimated transition matrix (rows=from, they sum to 1)
standardError / lowerEndpointMatrix / upperEndpointMatrix: the SE + CI per element (confidenceLevel)
log_likelihood: the log-likelihood of the fit
steadyStates: the stationary distribution (a matrix; >1 row if there are several recurrent classes)
the mean first-passage time: the expected number of steps i->j (the diagonal is 0); absent, with mfpt_note, when the chain is not ergodic
is_irreducible / period: the irreducibility flag + the period (blank, with period_note, when it is not irreducible)
interpretation_traps: the fitter does NOT fail on a gap (it treats it as a separate state) and it accepts a single state — the wrapper's gates block both explicitly
steadyStates returns a MATRIX: >1 row means several closed recurrent classes (a non-unique stationary distribution)
the period computation emits a WARNING rather than an error on a non-irreducible chain -> the wrapper returns a blank plus a note; do not interpret an invalid value
the mean first-passage time requires an ergodic (irreducible) chain -> otherwise it is absent, with a note, rather than an error that would crash the node
method='bootstrap' is STOCHASTIC (resampling CI) -> use the same seed for reproducibility; mle/laplace are deterministic
sources: Spedicato 2017 (discrete-time Markov chains: estimation and analysis)
Norris 1997, Markov Chains (CUP) — the stationary distribution, first passage, periodicity
precondition_tools: mc_fit (it produces the fitted chain, the input to mc_analytics)
c00_data_utilities/reading_delimited_fixed.read_delimited (loading the state sequence from a file)

cards.when: the autocorrelation of squared returns decays hyperbolically rather than exponentially, which no GARCH or IGARCH can reproduce
cards.when_not: the persistence is due to neglected structural breaks, which mimic long memory almost exactly; the sample is too short to distinguish the two

alternatives.criterion: persistence is exponential
shocks are fully permanent
the long memory is spurious and driven by breaks

output_key_fields: params: including d, the fractional differencing parameter
d: between 0 and 1 for genuine long memory
forecast_variance: which decays hyperbolically
loglike, aic, bic
interpretation_traps: STRUCTURAL BREAKS MASQUERADE AS LONG MEMORY -- an estimated d near 0.4 is entirely consistent with a stable process containing two variance breaks
FIGARCH is not covariance stationary for many parameter values yet still has a well-defined conditional variance; the usual stationarity intuition does not carry
the infinite lag polynomial must be truncated, and the truncation length affects both estimates and forecasts
sources: Baillie, Bollerslev & Mikkelsen 1996 (Journal of Econometrics 74:3-30)
Davidson 2004 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 22:16)
arch

cards.when: a one-parameter variance recursion that needs no estimation -- the industry default for fast risk updates
cards.when_not: you want a model whose parameters are estimated and testable; the series has strong mean reversion in volatility that EWMA cannot capture

alternatives.criterion: you want mean reversion and estimated parameters
speed and no estimation
intraday data available

output_key_fields: variance: the EWMA conditional variance path
lambda_: the decay factor used
half_life: the implied memory in periods
forecast: which is flat at all horizons
interpretation_traps: EWMA has NO MEAN REVERSION, so every multi-step forecast equals the current variance -- for long horizons this is badly wrong
the conventional decay factors of 0.94 daily and 0.97 monthly are conventions from one 1996 document, not estimates for your data
the recursion needs an initial variance, and with a short sample that choice persists into the estimates
sources: J.P. Morgan 1996, RiskMetrics Technical Document, 4th ed.
Alexander 2008, Market Risk Analysis II
arch

cards.when: combining a daily return model with a realised measure from intraday data, which reacts to volatility changes far faster than returns alone
cards.when_not: no intraday data is available; the realised measure is noisy enough that it adds variance rather than information

alternatives.criterion: no intraday data
a measurement equation links the two
separate dynamics for the return and realised components

output_key_fields: params: including the measurement-equation parameters
conditional_variance: the fitted path
measurement_residuals: which diagnose the realised measure's bias
loglike, aic
interpretation_traps: the measurement equation must account for the realised measure covering only TRADING HOURS while the return covers the full day; omitting that biases the level
a noisy realised measure degrades the model rather than improving it -- use a noise-robust estimator upstream
the leverage function is part of the measurement equation, so its parameters are not comparable with an EGARCH leverage term
sources: Hansen, Huang & Shek 2012 (Journal of Applied Econometrics 27:877-906)
Shephard & Sheppard 2010 (Journal of Applied Econometrics 25:197)

cards.method: High-frequency jump tests: bipower variation and Lee-Mykland
cards.when: separating the continuous and jump components of price variation, which have different implications for risk and for option pricing
cards.when_not: the data are daily, where jumps cannot be separated from volatility; microstructure noise dominates at the sampling frequency used

alternatives.criterion: a daily test that jumps occurred
you need the individual jump times
you want a simple truncation-based separation

output_key_fields: jump_statistic, p_value: the daily test
jump_times: dated jumps, where the intraday test is used
continuous_variation, jump_variation: the decomposition
jump_share: proportion of total variation attributable to jumps
interpretation_traps: MICROSTRUCTURE NOISE inflates every jump test at high sampling frequencies and produces spurious jumps; the sampling interval is not a detail
the intraday periodicity of volatility must be removed first, or the opening and closing periods generate false jump detections
bipower variation is itself biased by jumps in finite samples, which is why the ratio statistics use corrections
sources: Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard 2006 (Journal of Financial Econometrics 4:1-30)
Lee & Mykland 2008 (Review of Financial Studies 21:2535)
DOI 10.1093/rfs/hhm056

cards.when: dating shifts in unconditional variance, which otherwise show up as spurious persistence in a GARCH model
cards.when_not: the variance is plainly stable; the series is short enough that the algorithm's asymptotics do not apply

alternatives.criterion: the classic iterated cumulative sums of squares
you want a modern penalised segmentation
you prefer latent regimes to dated breaks

output_key_fields: break_dates: the detected variance change points
segment_variances: the variance within each segment
n_breaks: how many were found
persistence_before_after: GARCH persistence with and without break dummies
interpretation_traps: IGNORING VARIANCE BREAKS INFLATES GARCH PERSISTENCE toward one; an estimated alpha+beta of 0.99 very often means unmodelled breaks rather than genuine near-integration
ICSS assumes independent observations and over-detects breaks when the data are conditionally heteroskedastic; the corrected versions exist for that
each detected break costs degrees of freedom; a segmentation with many short segments is fitting noise
sources: Inclan & Tiao 1994 (JASA 89:913-923)
Sanso, Arago & Carrion 2004 (Revista de Economia Financiera 4:32)

cards.when: the probability of leaving a regime depends on observable conditions, rather than being a constant the model estimates once
cards.when_not: there is no credible driver of the transition probabilities; the sample has too few switches to identify their dependence

alternatives.criterion: no driver available
an observable shifts the switching odds
the regime is determined by the observable rather than probabilistic

output_key_fields: transition_probabilities: the fitted time-varying probabilities
params: regime parameters and the transition equation coefficients
smoothed_probabilities: regime probabilities at each date
expected_duration: which now varies over time
interpretation_traps: identifying the transition equation needs ENOUGH SWITCHES; with two or three regime changes in sample the coefficients are estimated on almost nothing
the label-switching problem is worse here because the transition equation's sign flips with the labelling
the driver must be predetermined; using a contemporaneous variable makes the transition endogenous
sources: Filardo 1994 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 12:299-308)
Diebold, Lee & Weinbach 1994, Regime switching with time-varying transition probabilities (Nonstationary Time Series Analysis and Cointegration)
statsmodels

cards.method: Advanced stochastic volatility: log-normal, Heston and rough volatility calibration
cards.when: volatility is a latent process with its own shocks, which a GARCH -- where volatility is a deterministic function of past returns -- cannot represent
cards.when_not: a GARCH fits adequately and the extra estimation cost is not justified; the sample is too short for the latent process to be identified

alternatives.criterion: deterministic conditional variance, far cheaper
latent volatility with its own shock
the short-horizon behaviour needs a Hurst parameter below one half

output_key_fields: params: volatility-process parameters
latent_volatility: the filtered or smoothed volatility path
hurst: the roughness parameter, where a rough model is fitted
diagnostics: convergence of the sampler or filter
interpretation_traps: stochastic volatility models have NO CLOSED-FORM LIKELIHOOD; every estimate comes from simulation or filtering, and its convergence must be checked rather than assumed
GARCH and stochastic volatility parameters are not comparable -- persistence means different things in a deterministic and a latent recursion
rough volatility with a Hurst parameter well below one half makes standard discretisation schemes fail; a specialised scheme is required
sources: Kim, Shephard & Chib 1998 (Review of Economic Studies 65:361-393)
Gatheral, Jaisson & Rosenbaum 2018 (Quantitative Finance 18:933)
stochvolmodels
